output.review_comment:
The diff looks like a legitimate, generalizable fix rather than a hack tailored to specific test inputs — the three new branches map directly onto the three docstring rules called out in the PR description (preserve mixed-case/acronym words, always capitalize the last word, capitalize the word right after a colon), and none of the code special-cases literal strings that would only make sense for the exact test fixtures. The tests file was left untouched, as requested.

A couple of edge cases worth double-checking before merging (I can't run the suite from here, so please confirm CI is green):

1. **Rule ordering**: the mixed-case check (`any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:])`) runs *before* the small-word check. That means an all-caps small word like "OF" or "AND" appearing mid-title would be preserved as-is instead of lowercased, since it also satisfies "has an uppercase char after position 0." If the spec intends small words to always be lowercased mid-sentence regardless of casing, this could be a latent bug — just not one exercised by the current 9 tests apparently.
2. **`is_after_colon` is strict**: it only checks `words[index-1].endswith(":")`, so a colon followed immediately by a quote or other trailing punctuation (e.g. `Title:"Sub`) wouldn't be detected. Probably fine for the current spec/tests, but worth a mental note.

Neither of these contradicts the stated docstring rules as described, and the implementation is reasonably clean and readable. Assuming the agent actually ran the test suite and confirmed all 9 tests pass (as claimed), this is safe to merge. Recommend a follow-up look at the two edge cases above if the editorial spec later expands.
